## Observed failure and impact Post-merge CI on `c4f8fd618805f1c9a3805a3ce7510d160c1ee07f` failed the Node 22 second release gate because the packed admission documentation fixture could not remove its temporary `global/locks` directory. The documented commands and assertions had already succeeded. This is an actionable test-lifecycle reliability issue: successful package behavior can still produce a red release gate. Official evidence: [run 42091355341, Node 22 job 127469923851](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/actions/runs/42091355341/job/127469923851). At 2026-11-05T19:17:08Z, the parent test reports the child command: `/node/22.23.4/x64/bin/node --test --test-concurrency=2 test/admission-docs-install.test.ts` Child stdout first prints `packed guide: 2 commands passed offline (JSON/TOON)` and the artifact SHA-512, then fails with: `ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir '/jev-admission-docs-/global/locks'` The parent test is `Node packed admission smoke stays offline and logs an explicit Bun skip without Bun in PATH`. It makes the second gate finish with 447 passed and 1 failed, despite 100% coverage. The first npm gate passed 448/448 and production audit reported zero vulnerabilities. Although the failing step is named “Full Bun release gate,” `release:check` invokes npm/Node coverage, and this nested test intentionally excludes Bun from PATH. ## Exact source and expected behavior - [Packed documentation test lines 22–93](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/blob/c4f8fd618805f1c9a3805a3ce7510d160c1ee07f/test/admission-docs-install.test.ts#L22-L93): the fixture isolates `PM_GLOBAL_PATH` under scratch, runs npm/npx commands sequentially, verifies JSON/TOON receipts and unchanged tracker state, then logs success at line 92. Line 93 closes the HTTP fixture and calls `rmSync(scratch, { recursive: true, force: true })` with no configured retries. - [Parent runner lines 109–125](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/blob/c4f8fd618805f1c9a3805a3ce7510d160c1ee07f/test/admission-install-runner.test.ts#L109-L125): awaits the child process; its nonzero teardown result rejects before the explicit Bun-skip/output assertions. - [CI workflow](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/blob/c4f8fd618805f1c9a3805a3ce7510d160c1ee07f/.github/workflows/ci.yml): Node 22/26 matrix, npm gate followed by Bun install and Bun-command gate. - Source goal: [pm-jev-tokenizer-admission](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/blob/c4f8fd618805f1c9a3805a3ce7510d160c1ee07f/.agents/pm/features/pm-jev-tokenizer-admission.toon) and [merged PR #92](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/pull/92) require offline installed-command proof and Node-only coverage when Bun is unavailable. Expected: successful packed-command behavior remains a successful test once owned resources are shut down and temporary artifacts are removed within a bounded cleanup policy. Persistent cleanup errors must remain visible. Actual: a directory removal error turns the otherwise successful smoke into a release-gate failure. ## Investigation limits and ownership This is one observed official Node 22 failure, not a deterministic local reproduction. Final PR CI and post-merge Node 26 passed. The merge commit has the same Git tree (`86fc209bbeb795d91122d2251a83971aed2a1a0b`) as final PR head `689ba33caaa0ad832d29ccd2c9aada9d9fc4d0ae`. This does not establish merge-introduced code drift or a Node 22-only defect. The source/log establish the cleanup failure boundary, but do not identify which process or filesystem condition caused the directory to remain nonempty. A concurrent/late writer is a hypothesis, not a proven cause. No provider calls, dependency installation, broad local test rerun, or production mutation was performed for this investigation. Dedup checked all 96 initial all-status Jev issue/PR records and refreshed all 97 before filing, all 53 canonical PM item records at the tested tree, all-status issue/PR searches for ENOTEMPTY/cleanup/flaky/admission-docs, relevant returned PR discussions, and PR #92 review threads. No matching Jev cleanup issue or explicit cleanup owner was found. The feature remains in progress but does not record this failure. Issues #93/#94 and the dev-glob advisory are separate. Related precedent: [closed host chore pm-p5u6](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/main/.agents/pm/chores/pm-p5u6.toon) handled resilient temporary-root cleanup in the host's packed-install workflow and older ENOTEMPTY incidents. Reuse its established lifecycle approach where appropriate; it does not currently fix this new Jev fixture. ## Regression criteria 1. Preserve the unchanged offline JSON/TOON commands, receipt checks, no-inference/no-mutation assertions, explicit Bun skip, artifact checks, and existing gate thresholds. 2. Ensure owned processes/resources are finished before deletion; establish whether any child can outlive the awaited command before attributing the error to a particular producer. 3. Add a focused deterministic teardown regression: a recoverable ENOTEMPTY condition is retried within a finite bound; an exhausted or unrelated cleanup error is surfaced. Do not blanket-ignore deletion errors or add unbounded sleeps. 4. Verify focused packed documentation and Node-only runner tests, then both supported Node versions and existing npm/Bun-command gates on the final fix head. Record the exact head and results separately from this observed failure. --- ### GitHub comments (2) > **@coderabbitai[bot]** (2026-11-05T19:40:59Z) > > > > >
